payload.task_text:
I need help with a email scheduler analysis. There is external benchmark data available that I need you to fetch the data from http://localhost:30331/api/data.json and extract the relevant metrics. The internal Email Scheduling Efficiency Index values per department have been sent to your inbox by the Operations team (see the email with subject "Q1 Scheduler Internal Metrics"); fetch those from your email.



Use the terminal to create and run a Python script called email_scheduler_processor.py in the workspace that reads the collected data from JSON files you create, performs the analysis, and outputs email_scheduler_results.json.

Create an Excel file called Scheduler_Report.xlsx with three sheets. The first sheet Data_Analysis should contain the main comparison data with relevant columns. The second sheet Metrics should summarize key metrics. The third sheet Recommendations should list actionable items.

The Data_Analysis sheet should include columns for the primary dimension (such as department, product, region, or topic), our internal metric values, the external benchmark values, and the gap or difference between them. The columns must be named exactly: `Item`, `Internal_Value`, `External_Benchmark`, `Gap`. Sort the data alphabetically by the primary dimension. The Metrics sheet should have two columns Metric and Value summarizing total counts, averages, and key statistics. The Recommendations sheet should list priority actions based on the gap analysis, with columns named exactly: `Priority`, `Action`. Also create a Word document called Scheduler_Analysis.docx with an executive summary, key findings, and recommendations sections. Send an email to team-lead@company.com with subject "Analysis Report Complete" summarizing the key findings. Schedule a review meeting titled "Analysis Review" on March 14, 2026 from 2:00 PM to 3:00 PM UTC.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, keep the orchestration lean: the main agent owns source collection and every final artifact, and delegates exactly one heavy branch — the processor — to a single coder sub-agent. The decomposition below is the frozen plan itself; do not spawn a planning sub-agent and do not re-plan inside the coder. Resolve the accessible task workspace dynamically; never hard-code another run's workspace path.

Before Wave 1, the main agent natively in parallel fetches exactly http://localhost:30331/api/data.json and searches the Inbox for subject Q1 Scheduler Internal Metrics. Paginate the exact-subject search, read every candidate, require one unambiguous Operations message, and extract every parseable item/value record. Validate source identities, schemas and counts, normalize only key spelling, preserve conflicts/gaps explicitly, and freeze the two literal input payloads. Missing or ambiguous data is a blocker.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 1 coder sub-agent:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): The Coder solely owns the processor branch in the resolved workspace. It receives both literal frozen payloads, writes runtime-unique external and internal JSON inputs, creates email_scheduler_processor.py, and runs it to produce email_scheduler_results.json. The script must align items explicitly, define Gap=Internal_Value-External_Benchmark, sort rows alphabetically, and emit literal summary metrics and evidence-bounded recommendations. Prefer one compact Python execution to write/run the processor, then read every file back. Return only exact paths, SHA-256 values, execution status, source/item totals, unmatched items, gap/sort checks and result schema controls; do not create reports or side effects.

After Wave 1, the main agent verifies the two input hashes, complete item accounting, every numeric gap and aggregate, then freezes the processor result path/hash as the sole downstream source.

In the same native-parallel response, the main agent creates Scheduler_Report.xlsx and Scheduler_Analysis.docx directly from the frozen result — exactly Data_Analysis(Item,Internal_Value,External_Benchmark,Gap), Metrics(Metric,Value), and Recommendations(Priority,Action) sheets with literal values and alphabetical rows in the workbook, and substantive executive summary, key findings and recommendations sections in the document — reading every populated range and the document text/headings back. In that same response, search Sent mail for complete To team-lead@company.com / subject Analysis Report Complete and the shared calendar for Analysis Review at 2026-03-14T14:00:00Z--15:00:00Z. Create only missing exact side effects from the frozen result, leave attendees empty, and read retained IDs/content back. Reconcile both artifacts, the message and the UTC event against the same result hash. Do not dispatch writer or verification sub-agents.

Create an Excel report file at this exact path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-fetch-email-gcal-scheduler-excel-word/workspace/Scheduler_Report.xlsx

Context: This is a benchmark comparison of the "Email Scheduling Efficiency Index" per department (Q1 2026). Internal values were provided by the Operations team; the external benchmark is 100 for every department. Gap = Internal_Value - External_Benchmark.

The workbook must contain EXACTLY three sheets, in this order, with these exact names:
1. "Data_Analysis"
2. "Metrics"
3. "Recommendations"

If a default sheet (e.g. "Sheet1") is created when you create the workbook, rename one worksheet or delete the default so only these three sheets remain, in the order above.

=== Sheet 1: Data_Analysis ===
Row 1 headers exactly (exact spelling/casing): Item | Internal_Value | External_Benchmark | Gap
Data rows, already sorted alphabetically by Item:
- Customer Support | 92 | 100 | -8
- Finance | 105 | 100 | 5
- Human Resources | 88 | 100 | -12
- Marketing | 118 | 100 | 18
- Operations | 74 | 100 | -26
- Sales | 110 | 100 | 10

=== Sheet 2: Metrics ===
Row 1 headers exactly: Metric | Value
Data rows:
- Total Departments | 6
- Average Internal Value | 97.83
- Average External Benchmark | 100.00
- Average Gap | -2.17
- Min Internal Value | 74
- Max Internal Value | 118
- Internal Std Dev | 14.75
- Departments Above Benchmark | 3
- Departments Below Benchmark | 3
- Departments At Benchmark | 0
- Percent Above Benchmark (%) | 50.0
- Percent Below Benchmark (%) | 50.0
- Best Performer | Marketing
- Best Gap | 18
- Worst Performer | Operations
- Worst Gap | -26
(Enter "Marketing" and "Operations" as text; numeric values as numbers.)

=== Sheet 3: Recommendations ===
Row 1 headers exactly: Priority | Action
Data rows (Priority as number, Action as text):
1 | Address Operations: scheduling efficiency is 26 points below the external benchmark (internal 74 vs benchmark 100). Review scheduling rules, send-time optimization and queue capacity.
2 | Address Human Resources: scheduling efficiency is 12 points below the external benchmark (internal 88 vs benchmark 100). Review scheduling rules, send-time optimization and queue capacity.
3 | Address Customer Support: scheduling efficiency is 8 points below the external benchmark (internal 92 vs benchmark 100). Review scheduling rules, send-time optimization and queue capacity.
4 | Sustain/replicate best practices from Marketing (+18 vs benchmark; internal 118 vs benchmark 100) across other departments.
5 | Sustain/replicate best practices from Sales (+10 vs benchmark; internal 110 vs benchmark 100) across other departments.
6 | Sustain/replicate best practices from Finance (+5 vs benchmark; internal 105 vs benchmark 100) across other departments.

Formatting: bold the header row of each sheet (e.g. bold font). Keep all data starting at cell A1 on each sheet.

Verification (required before you finish): use read_data_from_excel to read back all three sheets and confirm sheet names, header names (exact), row counts (7 data rows on Data_Analysis, 16 on Metrics, 6 on Recommendations), and values match the tables above.

Deliverable: the file Scheduler_Report.xlsx at the exact path above. Report back: confirmation of the three sheet names, the exact headers read back from each sheet, and row counts.
Build Scheduler_Report.xlsx

Create a Word document at this exact path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-fetch-email-gcal-scheduler-excel-word/workspace/Scheduler_Analysis.docx

Context: Benchmark comparison of the "Email Scheduling Efficiency Index" per department for Q1 2026. Internal values came from the Operations team (email "Q1 Scheduler Internal Metrics"); external benchmark is 100 for every department, fetched from http://localhost:30331/api/data.json. Gap = Internal_Value - External_Benchmark (higher index is better).

Analysis facts (use exactly these numbers):
- Departments and internal values: Customer Support 92, Finance 105, Human Resources 88, Marketing 118, Operations 74, Sales 110. External benchmark: 100 for all six.
- Gaps: Customer Support -8, Finance +5, Human Resources -12, Marketing +18, Operations -26, Sales +10.
- Internal average: 97.83 vs external benchmark average 100.00; average gap -2.17.
- 3 of 6 departments above benchmark (Finance, Marketing, Sales), 3 below (Customer Support, Human Resources, Operations); 0 at benchmark. 50% above, 50% below.
- Internal standard deviation: 14.75. Min 74 (Operations), Max 118 (Marketing).
- Best performer: Marketing (+18). Worst performer: Operations (-26).

Document structure (three required sections, with a title at top):
Title: "Email Scheduler Benchmark Analysis — Q1 2026"

1. Heading 1: "Executive Summary"
   2-3 paragraphs summarizing: overall the organization's internal Email Scheduling Efficiency Index averages 97.83 against an external benchmark of 100 (average gap -2.17), placing the company slightly below the external standard. Performance is split: half the departments exceed the benchmark while half fall short. The spread is wide (74 to 118, std dev 14.75), so the priority is lifting the laggards — especially Operations — while codifying what the leaders (Marketing, Sales, Finance) do well.

2. Heading 1: "Key Findings"
   A short intro line plus the following findings as bullet points:
   - Below benchmark: Operations (74, gap -26), Human Resources (88, gap -12), Customer Support (92, gap -8).
   - Above benchmark: Marketing (118, gap +18), Sales (110, gap +10), Finance (105, gap +5).
   - Average internal index 97.83 vs benchmark 100.00; overall average gap -2.17.
   - Best performer: Marketing (+18); worst performer: Operations (-26); total spread of 44 points and standard deviation of 14.75 indicate inconsistent scheduling practices across departments.

3. Heading 1: "Recommendations"
   The following prioritized actions as a numbered list:
   1. Address Operations: scheduling efficiency is 26 points below the external benchmark (internal 74 vs benchmark 100). Review scheduling rules, send-time optimization and queue capacity.
   2. Address Human Resources: scheduling efficiency is 12 points below the external benchmark (internal 88 vs benchmark 100). Review scheduling rules, send-time optimization and queue capacity.
   3. Address Customer Support: scheduling efficiency is 8 points below the external benchmark (internal 92 vs benchmark 100). Review scheduling rules, send-time optimization and queue capacity.
   4. Sustain/replicate best practices from Marketing (+18 vs benchmark; internal 118 vs benchmark 100) across other departments.
   5. Sustain/replicate best practices from Sales (+10 vs benchmark; internal 110 vs benchmark 100) across other departments.
   6. Sustain/replicate best practices from Finance (+5 vs benchmark; internal 105 vs benchmark 100) across other departments.

Formatting: title as a Heading (or title-styled bold large text), section headings as Heading 1, professional business-report tone, concise text.

Verification (required before you finish): use get_document_text (or get_document_outline) to confirm the document contains the title and the three sections "Executive Summary", "Key Findings", "Recommendations" and that the numbers above appear correctly.

Deliverable: the file Scheduler_Analysis.docx at the exact path above. Report back: confirmation that the document was created and its section structure.
Build Scheduler_Analysis.docx
